newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT:Capel B&K lowers India ACC net.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT:Capel B&K lowers India ACC net.

text.p: Securities firm James Capel B&K said on Friday it lowered its 1996/97 (April-March) net forecast for Associated Cement Companies (ACC) to 840 million rupees from 1.19 billion.
"Although we are bullish on the company's long-term prospects, it will face pressure on margins in the short term," the firm said in a note to investors.
"We believe that at 1,000-1,150 rupee levels, the stock offers a good entry opportunity," Capel B&K said, advising investors to "buy on weakness."
ACC shares closed 2.75 rupees lower at 1,438 on the Bombay Stock Exchange on Friday.
The securities firm said poor realisations and rising costs would eat into ACC's profits during 1996/97.
"We feel the market has not fully discounted the poor performance this year...it is therefore likely to see sharp southward movement pre-announcement of results."
Capel B&K said the stocks would see a 39.5 percent growth in earnings in 1997/98, arising mainly from volume growth and operational efficiencies.
The firm said the federal budget for 1997/98 and the recently announced central bank policy for the first six months of that year, were likely to boost growth.
"As investment into infrastructure projects begins to materialise, the cement sector will be the biggest beneficiary," Capel B&K said.

"The industry, which has a surplus capacity, requires a demand kicker from the infrastructure sector, as delayed decision-making on these projects has led to capacity coming up ahead of the requisite demand."
The securities firm said as projects took off towards the end of 1997/98 and beyond, excess supply was likely to ease.
"On the realisation front, the second half of 1997/98 and the whole of 1998/99 will witness a revival in prices as corporate investments look up."
A recent Reuters poll of 28 leading broking firms forecast an average 58.05 percent fall in ACC's 1996/97 net to 951.37 million rupees.
